title: Sub-Milliwatt Neural Architectures and On-Device Continual Learning for Ubiquitous TinyML Systems
background:
The proliferation of always-on sensing devices (wearables, environmental monitors, smart agricultural nodes) has created unprecedented demand for neural inference at sub-milliwatt power envelopes. State-of-the-art TinyML frameworks such as MCUNet [1] and µNAS [2] have demonstrated that careful co-design of architecture and memory hierarchy can fit competitive vision and audio models within 256KB SRAM budgets, while works on integer-only training [3] have begun to push the frontier toward on-device learning. Recent advances in event-driven and sparse spiking architectures [4] further suggest that energy per inference can be reduced by 10-100x compared to dense MAC-based pipelines, particularly when paired with non-volatile compute-in-memory substrates.

Despite this progress, three fundamental gaps prevent ubiquitous deployment. First, existing sub-mW models are largely static: once deployed, they cannot adapt to distribution shift caused by sensor aging, user-specific signal characteristics, or changing environmental conditions, and naive fine-tuning induces catastrophic forgetting under the strict memory and energy constraints of MCUs [5]. Second, current model compression pipelines treat the sensor as a fixed front-end, ignoring opportunities for joint optimization of analog sampling rate, bit-depth, and downstream architecture, leaving substantial energy on the table [6]. Third, there is no principled theory linking activation sparsity, weight precision, and learning stability under bounded compute, making it difficult to predict when on-device adaptation will succeed or fail. Closing these gaps requires a unified framework spanning circuits, architectures, and learning algorithms tailored for the unique constraints of ubiquitous TinyML.
challenges: Designing neural architectures that sustain inference below 1 mW while preserving accuracy on multimodal time-series tasks, requiring co-optimization of mixed-precision quantization (≤4-bit), structured sparsity, and memory-aware operator scheduling within ≤512KB on-chip memory

Enabling on-device continual learning with forward and backward transfer under MCU-class constraints (no DRAM, no floating-point unit), including memory-efficient replay or regularization schemes that bound update energy to <10 mJ per adaptation episode without catastrophic forgetting

Developing sensor-adaptive compression pipelines that jointly optimize analog front-end parameters (sampling rate, ADC bit-depth, channel selection) with downstream model topology, including differentiable proxies for analog energy and noise that integrate with neural architecture search

Establishing theoretical bounds and convergence guarantees for low-precision (≤8-bit) gradient-based learning under non-IID streaming data, including conditions on activation sparsity and quantization noise that ensure learning stability on resource-constrained hardware

Building open benchmarks and reproducible measurement methodology for end-to-end energy, latency, and accuracy on representative ubiquitous-computing workloads spanning vision, audio, biosignal, and IMU modalities across heterogeneous MCU and accelerator platforms
